Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNoHeaderMap` fails because it expects `getHeaderMap()` to return null when the CSV data has no header defined explicitly or via the CSVFormat. The test input string "a,b,c\n1,2,3\nx,y,z" uses the default format (CSVFormat.DEFAULT) which does not define any header.

The current implementation of `CSVParser.getHeaderMap()` (lines 287-289) returns a new `LinkedHashMap` constructed from the field `headerMap` without checking if `headerMap` is null. This causes a NullPointerException (NPE) when `headerMap` is null, as the HashMap copy constructor cannot take a null argument.

Looking further, `headerMap` is initialized in the constructor of CSVParser (line 244) via the call to `initializeHeader()`. The `initializeHeader()` method (lines 324-352) sets `hdrMap` to null initially and only constructs a non-null map if the format's header is non-null. If the format does not specify a header, `hdrMap` remains null and is returned as null, assigning null to `this.headerMap`.

Thus, when no header is declared in the format, `headerMap` is left null. Then calling `getHeaderMap()` triggers an NPE due to trying to copy from the null map.

The failing test expects `getHeaderMap()` to return null in this case (no header). But the current code tries to wrap `headerMap` blindly in a LinkedHashMap constructor, causing NPE.

Hence, the root cause is that `getHeaderMap()` lacks null-checking for `headerMap`. It should check if `headerMap` is null and return null directly, or otherwise return a new LinkedHashMap copy.

The bug report confirms the NPE when calling `getHeaderMap()` on a CSVParser with no header map, matching the analysis here.

No other recent bug reports appear relevant.

In summary, the bug occurs because `getHeaderMap()` assumes `headerMap` is always non-null, but `initializeHeader()` can return null when no header is present, resulting in the NPE upon copying.

The fix should add a null-check in `getHeaderMap()` to avoid calling the LinkedHashMap constructor on null.

After fixing `getHeaderMap()`, the test `testNoHeaderMap` will pass because it will correctly return null when no header map exists.
